verses.text: Then Job answered:
"If only my anguish could be weighed and all my suffering placed on the scales!
It would weigh more than the sand of the seas. That's why my words have been rash.
The Almighty's arrows are lodged in me, and my spirit drinks their poison. God's terrors line up against me.
Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass? Does an ox bellow when it has feed?
Can you eat bland food without salt? Does the white of an egg have any flavor?
I can't bring myself to touch such things. They're like food that makes me sick.
If only I could have what I've asked for, if only God would grant what I long for,
if only God were willing to crush me, to let his hand loose and cut me off.
Then I'd still have this comfort. Even in pain that won't let up, I could rejoice that I haven't denied the words of the Holy One.
How much strength do I have left to keep waiting? What end can I look forward to that would make me patient?
Am I as strong as stone? Is my body made of bronze?
There's no help left in me. Any resource I had has been driven away.
A person who's about to give up should receive kindness from a friend, even if they've lost their reverence for the Almighty.
My brothers have been as unreliable as a seasonal stream, like channels that run dry.
They're dark with ice and full of melting snow.
Then the dry season comes, and they vanish. In the heat they disappear from their beds.
Caravans turn aside looking for them, go out into the wasteland, and perish.
The caravans from Tema look for them, and the travelers from Sheba wait for them.
They arrive full of confidence and are stunned and distressed.
Now you've turned out to be no help. You see something terrifying and draw back in fear.
Did I ever ask you to give me anything or pay for a gift out of your own wealth?
Did I ask you to rescue me from an enemy or buy my freedom from my oppressors?
Teach me and I'll be quiet. Show me where I've gone wrong.
Honest words can hit hard. But what have your accusations proved?
Are you trying to correct mere words, treating the speech of someone in despair as wind?
You'd even cast lots for an orphan and sell off your own friend.
Now please look at me. I wouldn't lie to your face.
Please reconsider. Don't judge me unfairly. Think again, because my cause is just.
Have I spoken unjustly? Can't I tell the taste of something wrong?"
